account: The instruction was: “A number, a financial line, a target or a named customer project does not by itself open a thesis; a customer's deployment plan is evidence to the supplier's demand and product theses unless it changes the supplier's own cash or credit risk.” I considered a binding-obligation candidate asking whether NVIDIA’s guarantees or repurchase commitments create a material obligation, but rejected it because the report describes the arrangements without establishing a signed, named obligation due within 18 months. The reported capacity guarantees and revenue share therefore did not meet the candidate-opening criteria on the information provided.

proposed.looks_at: Nvidia's binding rent-back and utilization-guarantee commitments under the AI Compute Partnership
proposed.question: Did Nvidia take on binding obligations to rent back idle GPUs or guarantee utilization for AI Compute Partnership deployments by 2026-07-03?

rungs.label: Yes
rungs.condition: Nvidia had taken on at least one binding rent-back or minimum-utilization obligation under the partnership by 2026-07-03.

rungs.label: No
rungs.condition: Nvidia had taken on no binding rent-back or minimum-utilization obligation under the partnership by 2026-07-03.

proposed.scope: AI Compute Partnership rent-back and minimum-utilization commitments
proposed.lost_if_folded: Whether Nvidia has taken on a direct, potentially contingent obligation to absorb idle-capacity risk, distinct from the effect of any resulting cloud revenue on FY2027 total revenue.
proposed.settled_by: Nvidia's executed AI Compute Partnership agreements or an Nvidia filing describing its binding rent-back and utilization-guarantee obligations.

account: The instruction was: “A binding_obligation: an obligation a universe company takes on in its own name (a guarantee, financing, an equity stake, a purchase commitment), due when its signing can be checked, at most 18 months out.” I considered asking whether Nvidia would take on those obligations by 2027-01-31, but rejected that later due date because the item reported the arrangement as already announced, so the relevant check was whether it had been signed by the item date, not a future forecast. My chosen 2026-07-03 date was the report date, rather than evidence of a separately verified signing date.
